prose: Sean Goedecke argues software engineers don't get to be Luddites about AI. The violence framing is real - an Indianapolis council member's house was shot up over datacenter support, Sam Altman's home was firebombed and then shot at - and anti-AI writers like Brian Merchant and Gavin Mueller have explicitly reclaimed the Luddite label, arguing the 19th-century machine-breakers were right.

His counter: for engineers, whose profession is the automation machine, Luddism is self-negating. Being righteously angry about AI is understandable, but the weavers' cry against inevitable and irresistible laws is not a position available to the people who build the looms.
highlights: Engineers don't get to be Luddites about AI, argues Goedecke.
Anti-AI violence is escalating: a council member's house shot up, Altman's home firebombed.
Anti-AI writers explicitly reclaim the Luddite label.
His point: Luddism is self-negating for people whose job is building the machines.
